newsitem.title: UK: British say no trace of dumped IRA mine.
newsitem.headline: British say no trace of dumped IRA mine.

text.p: British forces said on Tuesday they had found no trace of a landmine reported to have been dumped by IRA guerrillas near a Northern Ireland military base.

Security sources said more checks would be carried out in the area of Girdwood Barracks in north Belfast after a telephone caller using an Irish Republican Army codeword told a local radio station that the device had been left.
"We have searched but nothing has been found," a police spokeswoman said.
The caller, hinting that an attack had been aborted, said the mine was abandoned because civilians were nearby.
Security sources said they would tread warily in case of booby traps.

It was the second such alert in Northern Ireland in just over 48 hours and came just before the resumption of multi-party talks aimed at easing a 28-year conflict over British rule in Northern Ireland.
The IRA ended a six-week period of inactivity in the province on Saturday leaving a van packed with 500 kg (1,100 pound) of explosives in a built-up area in the west of Belfast.
In a telephone call to a radio station, an IRA caller said their "engineers" had disarmed one of their own landmines before abandoning it.
Police said a lengthy "clearance operation" had revealed that the warning was a trap, intended to lure security forces into an ambush. The cache did not explode.

The ending of the IRA lull and the murder of a policeman, kicked to death by pro-British Protestants on Sunday, have cast a long shadow over the resumption of the talks chaired by former U.S. senator George Mitchell.
At least 10 people have been held for police questioning about the officer's murder.
Sinn Fein is barred from talks because the party's IRA military ally has rejected international pleas for a ceasefire.
The IRA is pledged to end British control of the province and merge it in an all-Ireland state ruled from Catholic Dublin. Majority Protestants are determined to stay British.
